source.notes: This study presents the preliminary dynamic fragility outputs for a case study [1.5-2) MW capacity class onshore wind turbine gearbox, impacted by 3 s average wind gusts. Windstorms and gearboxes are amongst the leading sources of onshore wind turbine insurance claim payouts, yet the relationship between the two is not well understood. A gearbox dynamic fragility framework is developed to quantify the uncertainty in wind gust fragility at different stages of the gearbox's operational life. An anonymized, Cooke's method approach is used to elicit and to objectively aggregate exceedance probabilities from 11 respondents in the wind energy supply chain. Preliminary findings suggest that the probability of full gearbox replacement increases with both time-phased degradation and wind gust speed and aligns well with empirical reliability data. Compared to a 10 m s-1 wind gust, a 70 m s-1 wind gust increases the gearbox replacement probability by 13-14% between 0 and 15 years of operational life. The outputs highlight areas of uncertainty requiring further validation and set the foundation for the development of wind gust vulnerability functions, which quantify the insurance losses expected from wind gust events.
source.title: Judgment-Based Dynamic Fragility Assessment of Gearboxes to Extreme Weather Events: Preliminary Findings
